items.title: Show HN: Slop City, a FOSS game that embeds social media posts
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I created this game with Codex Astra and Astra subagents. It went remarkably well. SLOP CITY is an autobiographical first-person lounge that embeds my TikTok posts. I use it to market my Digilore podcast app which is in the Apple App store.
However this submission is not a shameless plug, only partially, because it's free and open source so I encourage everyone to download the code and ask Codex or another LLM to sync social media posts from any source. Or... try doing that by hand :)
Jus

items.title: Show HN: Explanations and follow-ons for OpenAI/math
items.contentSnippet:
The official openai/math repo is closed to issues, PRs, and discussion.
I made this app to share some explanatory videos that help us all make sense of the release, catalogue follow-ons and improvements that build on the openai research, and more broadly provide a set of community tools for distributed research.

items.title: Show HN: Forwarder.cc – Static-site forms sent to your inbox, pay per message
items.contentSnippet:
TL;DR: 12 years ago I built a service that forwards simple HTML forms to an email address. I've been procrastinating on finishing it ever since, until today. You point your form at it and every submission lands in your inbox. It runs on credits, 1 credit = 1 message, no subscription. Perfect for static websites.
—Hey folks, back around 2014, alongside my job as a software engineer, I was building a lot of static websites for my own clients, mostly small businesses that just wanted a simple site.

items.title: Show HN: CoolDock – a second Dock for macOS with live widgets and an MCP server
items.contentSnippet:
I always hated desktop widgets because I never see them. They sit behind every window I have open. Same problem with Notification Center, it's hidden away so I never use it.
The dock, however, is always there, it's already taking the real estate from the bottom of my screen, so why not add a second dock on the exact same real estate, that shows up as soon as the dock hides and vice versa, but not for apps - for widgets!

items.title: Show HN: RDST – A local agent that watches Postgres/MySQL for query regressions
items.contentSnippet:
We noticed during the course of many many years of DBA related work that fixes to database issues and queries are always reactive. An entire database can fall over extremely quickly when an unbounded query grows without warning.
Traditionally, DBAs hear complaints of slowness and follow a methodical process: 
- manually browse pg_stats or other database related performance internal tables 
- see which queries are slowest
- figure out what indexes are missing
- figure out which indexes are actual
